title: Coin change: fewest coins
summary: Solve every smaller amount first; each amount's best uses one last coin plus an answer already known.
note: Unlimited coins of each value. The answer is -1 if no combination makes the amount.

panels.label: dp[a]: fewest coins for amount a (INF = not possible yet)

narration.text: Use {INF} as a marker for not possible: more coins than any real answer needs.
No amount is solved yet, so every entry starts at {INF}.
An amount of zero needs no coins: dp[0] = {dp[0]}.
Now find the fewest coins for amount {a}.
Every amount up to {amount} is solved.
Try a coin worth {c} as the last coin.
Every coin has been tried for amount {a}: the best is {dp[a]}.
That leaves {a - c}, which takes {dp[a - c]} coins, so {dp[a - c] + 1} coins in all, better than {dp[a]}.
A coin worth {c} is bigger than {a}: it can't be used.
Ending with {c} would take {dp[a - c] + 1} coins, no better than {dp[a]}.
Best so far for amount {a}: {dp[a]} coins.
No combination of coins makes {amount}, so there's no answer (the function returns minus one).
